## Phase 2: Initial Proposal

```
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
FEATURE SPEC PROPOSAL: API Readiness Endpoint
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Feature: API Readiness Endpoint
  As a load balancer or orchestration system
  I want to query the readiness endpoint
  So that I can determine when the API service is able to serve requests

  Background:
    Given the API service is running

━━ GROUP A: Key Examples (2 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Core path — verifies the readiness check returns the expected success signal
  @key-example @smoke
  Scenario: The service reports ready when able to serve requests
    When I request the readiness status with a GET request
    Then the readiness check should indicate the service is ready
    And the readiness response should identify the service as "api_test"

  # Why: Core restriction — confirms the endpoint is read-only and rejects mutations
  @key-example
  Scenario: Attempting to modify readiness state is rejected
    When I send a POST request to the readiness endpoint
    Then the request should be rejected as not allowed
    And the service should remain in a healthy state

━━ GROUP B: Boundary Conditions (4 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Exact boundary — the readiness status is a boolean, so "true" is the only positive value
  @boundary
  Scenario: The readiness indicator is reporting the exact required value
    When I request the readiness status with a GET request
    Then the readiness check should indicate the service is ready
    # [ASSUMPTION: confidence=high] Service name is 'api_test' and JSON body is fixed at {"ready": true, "service": "api_test"}
    And the readiness response should be exactly {"ready": true, "service": "api_test"}

  # Why: Just-inside boundary — a valid HTTP GET method is the only allowed request method
  @boundary
  Scenario: A GET request is the only accepted method for the readiness check
    When I send a GET request to the readiness endpoint
    Then the readiness check should be served successfully

  # Why: Just-outside boundary — a known disallowed method is clearly rejected
  @boundary @negative
  Scenario: A POST request is explicitly not allowed on the readiness endpoint
    When I send a POST request to the readiness endpoint
    Then the request should be rejected with a method not allowed status
    And the response should not indicate a successful operation

  # Why: Just-outside boundary — any request must be to the exact endpoint path
  @boundary @negative
  Scenario: A request to a different path is not treated as a readiness check
    When I send a GET request to a path other than "/ready"
    Then the request should not report the readiness of the service

━━ GROUP C: Negative Cases (2 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Negative validation — ensures the response is not accidentally a different method's response
  @negative
  Scenario: A non-GET, non-POST method is not supported for the readiness check
    When I send a PUT request to the readiness endpoint
    Then the request should be rejected as an unsupported method

  # Why: Negative validation — malformed requests should not affect the readiness state
  @negative
  Scenario: A request with an invalid content type is rejected
    Given I intend to send a POST request to the readiness endpoint
    And the request has an invalid content type
    When I send the POST request to the readiness endpoint
    Then the request should be rejected as not allowed

━━ GROUP D: Edge Cases (0 scenarios) ━━

No additional edge cases proposed for initial specification given the simplicity and strict requirements of the endpoint.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Total: 8 scenarios across 4 groups
Inferred assumptions: 4 (will be resolved in Phase 5)

```
